name: hazel_weir_central_procedural_graph
description: Optimized Central Procedural Graph featuring Day-30 Town Shop arbitrage, maturation-gated procurement, two-tier cyclical liquidation, zero-animal feed reserve unlocking, disciplined land scaling, and cluster-harvest worker dispatch.

nodes.name: State & Balance Audit
nodes.description: Computes net available cash, shed fill percentage, wage liability, active shop contract demand, and oracle price drop signals across market commodities.

nodes.name: Midnight Wage Reserve Defense
nodes.description: Protects payroll for all active hired hands. Enforces dynamic cash reserve locks and triggers pre-midnight surplus liquidation to prevent the 0-hand bankruptcy cascade.

nodes.name: Town Shop Demand Arbitrage
nodes.description: Preemptively matches unlocked town shop demand surges and immediately fulfills mature high-margin crops (Carrots, Tomatoes, Pumpkins, Strawberries) to capture 2.0x-3.5x contract price premiums.

nodes.name: Shed Headroom Relief
nodes.description: Prevents silent 100/100 harvest discards by clearing uncommitted low-margin inventory under strict price floors while protecting animal feed and shop contracts.

nodes.name: Oracle Opponent Front-Run
nodes.description: Reads 96-step TTM forecast to dump sensitive commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) immediately before opponent market gluts collapse prices.

nodes.name: Capital Reinvestment & Yield Scaling
nodes.description: Reinvests surplus cash beyond wage reserves into workforce acceleration (10-hand rush), contiguous land expansion, commercial high-yield seeds, and fertilizer.

nodes.name: Routine Farm & Workforce Execution
nodes.description: Executes field routines with strict operational sequencing: harvest ready crops, worker drop-offs, watering, livestock feeding, planting, and ground maintenance.

attributes.guidance: Cancel non-essential purchases (BUY_SEED, BUY_ANIMAL, BUY_LAND, redundant HIRE); schedule worker harvest drop-offs before hour 21; enforce emergency liquidation of non-feed, non-contract inventory at hour >= 20 to guarantee payroll.
attributes.pitfalls: Never sell Wheat below dynamic livestock feed reserve (n_animals > 0 ? n_animals * 3 : 0); when holding zero livestock (n_animals == 0), reserve zero Wheat and liquidate all early harvest to accelerate Day 1-4 hand hiring; do not rely on low-margin fertilizer sales to cover payroll deficits; never liquidate crops committed to active town shop delivery.

attributes.guidance: Preempt routine market sales by delivering matching mature shed inventory directly to town shops for 2.0x-3.5x contract price premiums throughout all 30 days (up to step 718); procure shop-demanded seeds strictly within crop maturation horizons (halt Pumpkin seeds after Day 23, Tomato seeds after Day 25, and Carrot seeds after Day 27) when net cash covers seed costs and wage reserves.
attributes.pitfalls: Never halt town shop contract deliveries after Day 28—continue fulfilling profitable contracts through Day 30; do not purchase shop seeds past their crop maturation cutoff dates; do not commit seed capital if net cash drops below 1.15x midnight payroll reserve; do not purchase seeds if shed capacity exceeds 88%.

attributes.guidance: Evict pending non-urgent buy orders to free order slots; execute batch sales of unreserved, non-shop surplus inventory with a strict primary price floor of >= 0.85 * base_price; only relax the liquidation floor to 0.50 * base_price if shed_used >= 94 to definitively eliminate silent 100/100 harvest discards.
attributes.pitfalls: Never fire-sell below 0.85x base price unless shed_used >= 94 overflow is imminent; never liquidate Wheat below dynamic feed reserve (n_animals > 0 ? n_animals * 3 : 0); 100% of Wheat is liquidatable when n_animals == 0; never evict produce allocated for active town shop fulfillment.

attributes.condition: (oracle_glut_risk >= 0.25 and current_price >= 0.85 * base_price) or (uncommitted_crop_inventory >= 6 and current_price >= 1.05 * base_price)
attributes.guidance: Preempt low-priority open orders; liquidate uncommitted surplus inventory during cyclical market price peaks (>= 1.05 * base_price) to capture peak margins and recycle liquid capital, or front-run predicted opponent market gluts (oracle_glut_risk >= 0.25 and current_price >= 0.85 * base_price) for sensitive commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry, mature crops) before opponent dumping depresses market pricing.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not sell into depressed market troughs (< 0.85x base price) unless critical shed overflow occurs; never liquidate produce committed to active Town Shop contracts or required for dynamic livestock feed (n_animals > 0 ? n_animals * 3 : 0).

attributes.condition: ((day <= 8 and hired_hands < 10 and net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.10 + 80.0) or (day > 8 and hired_hands < 10 and net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.25 + 150.0) or (net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.25 + 180.0 and ((uncultivated_plots <= 1 and plots_owned < 22 and day <= 22) or (has_fertilizer_deficit and day <= 25)))) and day <= 26
attributes.guidance: Front-load workforce hiring to reach the 10-hand maximum by Day 6-8 utilizing the lowered $80 buffer on Days 1-8. Expand cultivation acreage contiguously whenever plots are fully planted (uncultivated_plots <= 1) up to a disciplined 20-22 plot maximum by Day 22. Procure high-margin commercial seeds (Pumpkins, Tomatoes, Strawberries) and fertilizer to maximize harvest yields per plot.
attributes.pitfalls: Never over-expand land beyond 22 plots where hands cannot maintain watering and harvesting; halt land purchases after Day 22 and hand hiring after Day 20; never allocate capital if net cash after purchase drops below the required payroll buffer.

attributes.guidance: Dispatch active hands with cluster-optimized field sequencing: 1) Cluster harvest adjacent mature crops until inventory reaches >= 2 items (or backpack full) or local cluster is exhausted before pathing to shed; 2) Drop off carried items at shed upon reaching backpack capacity, tool swap, or during mandatory pre-midnight drop-off window (hour >= 20); 3) Water dry cultivated crops; 4) Feed hungry livestock (if n_animals > 0); 5) Plant commercial/shop seeds; 6) Weed clearing and ground tilling. Ensure all carried inventory is deposited at shed by step 716 for terminal liquidation.
attributes.pitfalls: Never send a hand trekking to the shed with only 1 item if adjacent mature crops remain unharvested in the local cluster; never permit hands to carry uncommitted inventory past hour 21 into midnight payroll; never prioritize weeding over harvesting or watering; ensure hands never idle while unharvested crops or dry plots remain.
